TIL that in 1881, Fanny Hesse suggested growing bacteria on agar, a jelly ingredient from her own kitchen, because the gelatin in her husband's experiments kept melting in the summer heat. Agar is still the standard in labs worldwide, and she never got credit for the idea.

TIL in 1982, 19 year old UT student Gregory Watson wrote a paper about how a 1789 Amendment to the Constitution was never ratified. The TA and professor gave him a C Grade. He campaigned for it and in 1992 the amendment was ratified. 35 years later his C was changed to an A.

TIL in the 1970s, Toronto Maple Leafs owner Harold Ballard refused to put names on jerseys as he wanted fans to buy game programs to identify players by number. When the NHL mandated names in 1977, he rebelled by printing blue names on blue (and white on white) before finally being forced to comply.
TIL that in 2019, a Canadian woman scared off a cougar approaching her and her dog by playing Metallica's “Don’t Tread on Me” on her cellphone after shouting failed to deter it.

TIL in Germany, they have something called a frauenparkplatz, parking spots dedicated to women, closer to exists, in areas with more surveillance and better lighting for safety. They are also sometimes wider.

TIL The Code of the U.S. Fighting Force is a code of conduct that is an ethics guide consisting of six articles to members of the United States Armed Forces, addressing how they should act in combat and when they must evade capture, resist while a prisoner or escape from the enemy.

TIL in 1980, after Republicans failed to nominate a candidate for a U.S. House seat in New Mexico, Joe Skeen launched a write-in campaign and won with 61,564 votes. He became just the third person in American history elected to the U.S. House as a write-in candidate. He served for 22 years.
